newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk judges attend army talk despite Islamist call.
newsitem.headline: Turk judges attend army talk despite Islamist call.

text.p: Top members of Turkey's judiciary attended a briefing on religious activism by the powerful military on Tuesday, defying an order from the Islamist justice minister to stay away from the meeting.
Several hundred judges and prosecutors packed a meeting hall at military headquarters despite a warning from Justice Minister Sevket Kazan of investigations into those attending the talks.

The dispute, covered widely by the secularist media, marked the latest round of a festering row between the military and the 11-month-old Islamist-led coalition over army-led demands for a government crackdown on religious activism.
The justice ministry said the judicial officials had been sent a written request not to attend the meeting.

"The ministry's personnel office has sent a written request to the chief prosecutor's office saying it is inappropriate for judges and prosecutors to participate in the briefing," a ministry official told Reuters.
Speaking in parliament, Islamist Welfare Party member Kazan said the demand had been made because permission to attend had not been sought from him.
"If they get permission from the justice minister they can participate. Otherwise it is impossible for them to take part," state-run Anatolian news agency quoted Kazan as saying.
The secularist army and Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party have been engaged in a fierce battle since February when the National Security Council ordered curbs on resurgent Islamism.
Among their demands were measures aimed at restricting the role of religious schools and closing unofficial Koran courses.

Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, has stalled on implementing the council's demands and announced on June 1 that his coalition with conservatives would seek early elections to resolve the row. No date for the polls has been set.
The military, which described the battle with Islamists as a matter of life or death at an earlier press briefing, is scheduled to brief the media on the same subject on Wednesday.
